description:
medium-tier-ci-home (DONE, PR #952) gave the ~81-file medium speed tier its
first CI consumer: the `medium-test` job in
.github/workflows/develop-post-merge.yml (lines ~74-113), deliberately
visibility-only (`continue-on-error: true`, excluded from
auto-revert-on-failure's needs/if) because the tier was known-red. The
recorded promotion criterion: a full clean green run of `make test-medium`,
with two named prerequisites — (1) regenerate the stale
cross-surface-applicability artifact (DONE: PR #952 commit 3d64c58e
regenerated it, so tests/unit/test_cross_surface_applicability.py::
test_committed_artifact_is_current may already pass), and (2) a
clean-environment re-measurement to disposition the "14 failures / 44
errors" previously observed only under a contended sandbox.

LIVE EVIDENCE the tier is still red on clean develop: on the #952 squash
itself (fddedf26, develop-post-merge run 28706929881, 2026-07-04), the
medium-test job FAILED on a real GitHub runner (job 85134046869-series,
"Run medium speed tier" step failure at 13:07 UTC) while lint and
fast-test passed. The job behaved exactly as designed (no block, no
auto-revert), but the promotion criterion is now measurably unmet on
uncontended hardware — so the remaining work is real failure disposition,
not just re-measurement.

anti_patterns.dont: disposition failures by blanket-adding skip markers
anti_patterns.instead: every skip/re-tier needs a one-line justification naming what would make it runnable.

anti_patterns.dont: promote with continue-on-error still set 'to be safe'
anti_patterns.instead: the two flips go together or not at all.
anti_patterns.why: a non-blocking auto-revert trigger is a contradiction (the if-expression would never see failure)

preserves.behavior: The medium tier's ~18-minute runtime envelope: dispositions must not quietly move slow tests INTO the fast (PR-blocking) tier as a shortcut.
auto-revert-on-failure's current behavior for lint/fast-test/explorer-tokens (including its outputs consumed by metrics) — promotion adds a trigger, it must not restructure the job.

prior_art.concept: .github/workflows/develop-post-merge.yml:medium-test job comment — reuse: it prescribes the exact promotion mechanics (drop continue-on-error, add medium-test to auto-revert-on-failure's needs + if, mirroring lint/fast-test).
_project/DONE/main/medium-tier-ci-home.yaml — the measurement history and known-red inventory this TODO dispositions; extend its accounting rather than re-deriving it.

tests/unit/workflows/test_develop_post_merge_metrics.py — extend: the pinned tests for develop-post-merge wiring; promotion must update whichever assertions pin medium-test's exclusion from auto-revert.

verifications.expected: all pass with medium-test asserted inside auto-revert-on-failure's needs/if

work_units.notes:
Fetch the failing-test list from develop-post-merge run 28706929881's
medium-test job logs (gh api / MCP get_job_logs), or trigger a fresh
run's logs if expired. Summarize: N failures / M errors, grouped by
module, with the one-line error per group, into this TODO's notes.
This replaces the stale "14 failures / 44 errors under contention"
figure with clean-runner truth.
DONE 2026-07-05 (mcp get_job_logs, job 85134046886, run 28706929881):
8 failed / 1282 passed / 5 skipped in 582.75s. Groups:
  A. pytest-timeout >60s (6): amplab/coffeeshop/read-primitives
     cross-surface dataframe-equivalence tests;
     ssb/clickbench/h2odb TestX::test_generate_data. All are real
     slow tests (data-gen loops / dual-surface execution), killed by
     the medium lane's --timeout=60, not hangs.
  B. real failures (2):
     - test_no_new_raw_print_in_benchbox_runtime: raw print() in
       cross_surface.py, tpchavoc/equivalence.py,
       tpchavoc/dataframe_equivalence.py (report __main__ output)
       not in _PENDING_MIGRATION;
     - test_display_results: CaptureResult(out='') under -n 5 -
       global set_quiet(True) leaked from an earlier test in the
       same worker (reproduced + mutation-probed locally).
work_units.summary: Pull the authoritative failure list from the live red run (not a contended local run)

work_units.notes:
For each failure group decide and act: fix small real bugs in-scope
here; file separate TODOs for large ones (link them in deps of the
promotion unit); re-tier tests that genuinely need resources the
runner lacks (marker change, with justification); delete/repair stale
assertions. Confirm whether test_committed_artifact_is_current now
passes post-3d64c58e and strike prerequisite (1) if so.
DONE 2026-07-05:
  - Group A (6 timeouts): per-test @pytest.mark.timeout markers
    (300s for ssb/clickbench/amplab measured 42-58s; 600s for
    h2odb/coffeeshop/read-primitives measured 246-257s in a 4-core
    container). Kept IN the medium lane (not re-tiered to slow)
    because the slow lane's only consumer, release-canary, is not
    yet activated (release-canary-scheduled-activation w2 pending)
    - re-tiering now would move them from red-but-visible to
    not-run-at-all. Marker overrides the CLI --timeout=60 per
    pytest-timeout precedence. Revisit tiering once the canary runs.
  - Raw-print (1): the three report-entrypoint modules added to
    _PENDING_MIGRATION with justification (pre-existing prints;
    cross_surface.py is a CODEOWNERS soundness path, so the emit()
    migration belongs in a reviewed comparator PR).
  - Quiet-leak (1): autouse _reset_global_quiet_state fixture in
    tests/conftest.py resets set_quiet(False) after every test;
    leak scenario reproduced and mutation-probed (fixture off ->
    exact CI failure; on -> green).
  - Prerequisite (1) STRUCK: test_committed_artifact_is_current
    passes on develop post-3d64c58e (verified 2026-07-05).
work_units.summary: Disposition every failure: real bug, stale test, environment-dependency, or marker misplacement

work_units.notes:
